samples.summary: Unconditional `fetchMe` in CollabDocumentProvider logs out and redirects anonymous share-link visitors to /login
samples.evidence: `CollabDocumentProvider` now runs `useQuery({ queryKey: ['me'], queryFn: fetchMe, retry: false })` on every mount (line 152-156). `fetchMe` (api/auth.ts:116) goes through `fetchWithAuth`, which on a 401 that refresh cannot fix calls `logout({redirect:false,...})` and `redirectTo("/login")` — i.e. `window.location.href = '/login'` (api/auth.ts:220-227). `shared-document.tsx` renders `CollabDocumentProvider` for doc/slides/note/board/sheet share links (lines 979, 998, 1007, 1022, 1035) and `app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:200` does too (mounted by `SharedPdfLayout`). Those routes are public and their own identity query is `['me','optional']` with `fetchMeOptional` (shared-document.tsx:901), so the new `['me']` query is a cache miss and actually fires. An anonymous visitor to any public share link therefore gets a 401, a forced logout and a navigation to /login — the share view never renders. This fires regardless of the offline preference, which is never even set anywhere in app code.

samples.summary: `LossWatch` calls `useDocument()` above the `DocumentProvider`, so the loss latch can never be set (or the render throws)
samples.evidence: In `DurableYorkieProvider` the tree is `KeyedYorkieProvider > LockRefusalWatch > LossWatch > {children}`, and `children` is `inner` from collab-document-provider.tsx:163-168 — which *is* the `DocumentProvider`. So `LossWatch`'s `useDocument()` (line 122) runs outside any `DocumentProvider`. Either the hook throws (crashing every durable document) or `doc` is undefined, the `useEffect` returns early (line 125), and `store.expectLoss(...)` is never called. Without the latch, `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` treats every removal as an ordinary detach and deletes the entry instead of archiving it — the unsent work the whole offline-copy path exists to hand back is silently destroyed. The durable test suite mocks `@yorkie-js/react`'s `useDocument` to always return a doc (collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:31-40), so it cannot detect this.

samples.summary: Share links are NOT structurally excluded: a signed-in visitor gets a durable client with the wrong auth token
samples.evidence: The docstring at lines 137-140 asserts "`shared-document.tsx` mounts its own provider, so anonymous share links are excluded structurally". They are not: shared-document.tsx:979-1042 renders `CollabDocumentProvider` inside its share-token `YorkieProvider`. For a *signed-in* visitor on someone else's share link, `me` is defined, `isExcluded` (use-durable-document.ts:31) only refuses `pdf-` keys, so with the preference on the durable path mounts a nested `DurableYorkieProvider` with `authTokenInjector={fetchYorkieToken}` (collab-document-provider.tsx:198) instead of `fetchYorkieShareToken(token)` (shared-document.tsx:976). The attach then carries the user's own credential, which they may not have for that document — the share view breaks — and the share document is persisted to disk under `wb:{userId}:{docKey}` regardless.

samples.summary: Quota eviction selects victims across all users, deleting another account's unsent work on a shared device
samples.evidence: `evictOldest` builds candidates from `headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, IDBKeyRange.lowerBound(-Infinity))` (lines 981-984), which is the `updatedAt` index over *every* header row in the origin database, with no `userId` filter. The rest of the class is scrupulous about scoping (`dropAllForUser` filters by `BY_USER`, `listArchives`/`loadArchive` refuse other users' rows), and the class docstring for `dropAllForUser` says signing out of one account "must not destroy another's unsent work" — but a single quota-pressured `saveSnapshot` by user A will `purge` user B's oldest entry, unsent log included. `collectStale`'s `dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` (line 839) is likewise unscoped.

samples.summary: `durable` is never passed to `deriveSyncState`, so `saved-locally` is unreachable and durable documents still report "Not saved"
samples.evidence: `deriveSyncState` gained a `durable` signal (sync-state.ts:70,85) and the chip gained a `saved-locally` label/icon/tooltip, but the only production caller is `use-sync-status.ts:214`, which passes `{ connected, pending, syncFailed }` and nothing else, so `durable` always defaults to `false`. The new state is dead in the app: a document whose unsent edits are on disk still shows the destructive "Not saved" chip. This also breaks the invariant the PDF exclusion is justified by in use-durable-document.ts:26-29 ("whatever is durable must be reportable").

samples.summary: `watchForOfflineDisable` and `collectStale` are never invoked from application code, so the "turning this off deletes them" promise and the 30-day sweep never run
samples.evidence: A grep for `watchForOfflineDisable`, `collectStale`, `eraseOfflineData`, `listRecoverableWork`, `recoverOfflineCopy` and `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled` finds matches only inside `src/lib/*.test.*` and the modules themselves — no route, no Settings page, no app bootstrap. So nothing ever sets the preference, nothing installs the disable watcher, and nothing schedules stale collection. The store's own comments call an uncollected archive store "a quota leak that looks like a feature" (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:837-838) and offline-erase.ts:13 quotes Settings copy that does not exist yet. If the preference is ever flipped by hand (localStorage), documents accumulate forever with no collection and no erase.

samples.summary: `remove()` consumes the loss latch before the transaction commits and is not wrapped in `atomically`
samples.evidence: `remove()` (lines 663-706) deletes the latch with `this.expectedLosses.delete(documentKeyOf(docKey))` at line 681, then issues the archive `put` and three deletes, then awaits `completed(tx)` at line 704. Unlike `saveSnapshot`/`appendChange`/`saveMeta`, it does not use `WafflebaseDocStore.atomically`, so (a) if the archive `put` or any delete throws synchronously mid-sequence, the already-issued requests still commit — e.g. the snapshot deleted while the archive put never happened, which destroys the only copy of the unsent work; and (b) if the transaction aborts (quota is plausible here, since archiving doubles the entry's footprint and `remove` has no `withQuotaRetry`), the latch has already been consumed, so a retried removal will take the ordinary-detach path and delete without archiving.

samples.summary: `isOpenInAnyTab` matches only the document-key suffix, so another account's lock blocks this user's eviction/collection
samples.evidence: The suffix built at line 221 is `:${documentKeyOf(key)}` and the predicate only requires `startsWith('wb-durable:')`, so a lock named `wb-durable:other-user:note-7` matches a query for this user's `note-7`. Two accounts on one device that both have `note-7` open will each see the other's document as live, permanently refusing eviction and 30-day collection for that key. The user segment of the lock name is available and is not compared.

samples.summary: The store is memoized per component instance, so each open document does get its own `touched` set — contradicting the stated invariant
samples.evidence: The docstring (lines 61-64) says re-creating the store "per document would give each one its own `touched` set — which is how eviction ends up deleting a document another view is actively persisting", but `useMemo(..., [userId])` (lines 76-87) is per `DurableYorkieProvider` instance and one is mounted per `CollabDocumentProvider`, i.e. per document. Two durable documents open in the same tab therefore do have separate `touched` sets; correctness rests entirely on `isOpenElsewhere`/`isOpenInAnyTab`, which fails closed only because it returns `true` on error. Either the comment or the memo scope is wrong.

samples.summary: `standDown` performs a side effect (`session.release()`) inside a `setState` updater
samples.evidence: Lines 144-152 call `current.session.release()` from within the `setDecision` updater. React may invoke updaters more than once (StrictMode, or a re-render during concurrent rendering), so the release runs more than once; it is idempotent per caller via the `released` flag in durable-session.ts:174, so the impact is contained, but an impure updater is a latent hazard if that idempotence is ever relaxed.

samples.summary: IndexedDB connections are opened per document store instance and never closed
samples.evidence: `WafflebaseDocStore.close()` (line 404) exists but is called nowhere — `DurableYorkieProvider` creates a store in `useMemo` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:76) and has no cleanup effect that closes it on unmount. Every durable document opened in a session leaves an open `IDBDatabase` connection behind. `onversionchange` mitigates a cross-tab `deleteDatabase` block, but the connections themselves accumulate for the life of the tab.

finding.summary: Unconditional `fetchMe` in CollabDocumentProvider logs out and redirects anonymous share-link visitors to /login
finding.evidence: `CollabDocumentProvider` now runs `useQuery({ queryKey: ['me'], queryFn: fetchMe, retry: false })` on every mount (line 152-156). `fetchMe` (api/auth.ts:116) goes through `fetchWithAuth`, which on a 401 that refresh cannot fix calls `logout({redirect:false,...})` and `redirectTo("/login")` — i.e. `window.location.href = '/login'` (api/auth.ts:220-227). `shared-document.tsx` renders `CollabDocumentProvider` for doc/slides/note/board/sheet share links (lines 979, 998, 1007, 1022, 1035) and `app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:200` does too (mounted by `SharedPdfLayout`). Those routes are public and their own identity query is `['me','optional']` with `fetchMeOptional` (shared-document.tsx:901), so the new `['me']` query is a cache miss and actually fires. An anonymous visitor to any public share link therefore gets a 401, a forced logout and a navigation to /login — the share view never renders. This fires regardless of the offline preference, which is never even set anywhere in app code.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the working tree. collab-document-provider.tsx:152-156 issues an unconditional useQuery({queryKey:['me'], queryFn: fetchMe, retry:false}) with no `enabled` guard. fetchMe (api/auth.ts:116-123) goes through fetchWithAuth, which on a 401 that refresh cannot fix calls logout({redirect:false,...}) and redirectTo("/login") (api/auth.ts:213-228), and redirectTo assigns window.location.href (api/auth.ts:53-62). Public share routes mount this component: shared-document.tsx:979/998/1007/1022/1035 (inside SharedDocumentInner, a public token route) and files/pdf-collab.tsx:199. Those routes' own identity query uses the distinct key ["me","optional"] with fetchMeOptional (shared-document.tsx:900-904), so the new ['me'] query is a cache miss and genuinely fetches. The backend /auth/me is @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard) (backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:61-65), so an anonymous visitor gets 401 and no refresh cookie exists. Result: anonymous share-link visitors are logged out and hard-navigated to /login instead of seeing the shared document. The component's own comment (collab-document-provider.tsx:138-140) claiming shared-document.tsx "mounts its own provider" so share links are "excluded structurally" is contradicted by shared-document.tsx:979 ff. I found no guard, route condition, or QueryClient default anywhere that makes this unreachable; all other queryKey ["me"] call sites (PrivateRoute.tsx:13, app-sidebar.tsx:61, the five detail routes) are authenticated-only. Critical: breaks a core public flow.

No guard makes this unreachable; it is on the normal durable-document path. Critical under the correctness rubric: crash on a real path and/or loss of unsent user work.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: shared-document.tsx:979-1042 renders CollabDocumentProvider inside its share-token YorkieProvider (authTokenInjector=fetchYorkieShareToken at shared-document.tsx:976), so the docstring claim at collab-document-provider.tsx:137-140 (and docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:233-234) that share links are 'excluded structurally' is false. use-durable-document.ts:31-33 excludes only 'pdf-' keys, and eligibility (use-durable-document.ts:78-79) has no share-context term; share docKeys are doc-/slides-/note-/board-/sheet- (shared-document.tsx:960-969). finding.summary: Quota eviction selects victims across all users, deleting another account's unsent work on a shared device
finding.evidence: `evictOldest` builds candidates from `headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, IDBKeyRange.lowerBound(-Infinity))` (lines 981-984), which is the `updatedAt` index over *every* header row in the origin database, with no `userId` filter. verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described and is reachable. `evictOldest` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:980-1000) enumerates candidates with `headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, IDBKeyRange.lowerBound(-Infinity))`, i.e. every header row in the origin database, excluding only the key being written and `isLive` docs (987-988); there is no `userId` predicate even though `HeaderRecord.userId` (69) and the `BY_USER` index (349) exist. The victim is then `purge`d, which deletes the snapshot, header and the entire change log (717-725), so another account's unsent work is destroyed. Multi-user coexistence in one database is real: `dbName` defaults to the fixed `DEFAULT_DB_NAME` (35, 296) and the app constructs the store without an override (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:78-86); the rest of the module is deliberately user-scoped (dropAllForUser 795-806, listArchives 736-747, loadArchive 758-773, offline-erase.ts:18-31) and a test asserts the shared-device invariant (wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts:83-103). No guard elsewhere makes the unscoped eviction unreachable — `isLive` reports openness, not ownership, so another account's idle entries are the preferred victims, and `this.evicted` (998) is per-instance so the other user's later session gets no loud failure. Silent cross-account data loss is in the Correctness lane.

finding.summary: `durable` is never passed to `deriveSyncState`, so `saved-locally` is unreachable and durable documents still report "Not saved"
finding.evidence: `deriveSyncState` gained a `durable` signal (sync-state.ts:70,85) and the chip gained a `saved-locally` label/icon/tooltip, but the only production caller is `use-sync-status.ts:214`, which passes `{ connected, pending, syncFailed }` and nothing else, so `durable` always defaults to `false`. This also breaks the invariant the PDF exclusion is justified by in use-durable-document.ts:26-29 ("whatever is durable must be reportable").

verdict.reason: The literal absence is real — use-sync-status.ts:214 is the only production caller of deriveSyncState and passes no `durable`, so `saved-locally` is currently unreachable — but the harmful behavior the finding asserts cannot fire. `durable` can never be true in this build: use-durable-document.ts:78-79 gates eligibility on supportsClientKey(), which reads the build-time pin (vite.config.ts:360-364) of @yorkie-js/react = 0.7.22 (package.json:65) against MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23 (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24), so atLeast() is false and `durable` (use-durable-document.ts:141) is constantly false. Consequently collab-document-provider.tsx:181-207 never mounts DurableYorkieProvider/WafflebaseDocStore, no unsent edit is ever on disk, the "not-saved" tooltip wording ("they exist only in this tab", sync-status-chip.tsx:88) stays accurate, and the PDF-exclusion invariant ("whatever is durable must be reportable", use-durable-document.ts:26-33) is not breached because nothing is durable. What is left is an unreachable branch behind a closed, documented feature gate (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:95-99,175) — a completeness gap, not a correctness defect on a reachable path, and therefore not blocking under this lens.

verdict.reason: The absence itself checks out — `watchForOfflineDisable` and `collectStale` have no non-test caller (my own repo-wide grep excluding *.test.* found only the definitions and docs). What does not hold is the consequence that makes it a correctness defect. The only production construction of WafflebaseDocStore is durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:76-87, reached solely from collab-document-provider.tsx:185-207 when `durable` is true; `durable` requires supportsClientKey() (use-durable-document.ts:78-79), which compares the build-injected @yorkie-js/react pin against MinClientKeyVersion "0.7.23" (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,61-67). The pin is 0.7.22 (packages/frontend/package.json:65, injected at vite.config.ts:354-362), so the gate is shut: even hand-flipping the localStorage preference leaves `eligible` false, no store is opened, nothing is written to IndexedDB, and there is nothing for a sweep to collect or an erase to delete. finding.summary: `remove()` consumes the loss latch before the transaction commits and is not wrapped in `atomically`
finding.evidence: `remove()` (lines 663-706) deletes the latch with `this.expectedLosses.delete(documentKeyOf(docKey))` at line 681, then issues the archive `put` and three deletes, then awaits `completed(tx)` at line 704. Unlike `saveSnapshot`/`appendChange`/`saveMeta`, it does not use `WafflebaseDocStore.atomically`, so (a) if the archive `put` or any delete throws synchronously mid-sequence, the already-issued requests still commit — e.g. the snapshot deleted while the archive put never happened, which destroys the only copy of the unsent work; and (b) if the transaction aborts (quota is plausible here, since archiving doubles the entry's footprint and `remove` has no `withQuotaRetry`), the latch has already been consumed, so a retried removal will take the ordinary-detach path and delete without archiving.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described. `remove()` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:663-706) consumes the loss latch at line 681 (`this.expectedLosses.delete(...)`) before the transaction commits at line 704, and issues its archive `put` (693) and three deletes (700-702) directly on `tx` without the `WafflebaseDocStore.atomically` wrapper that every other writer uses (touch:468, saveSnapshot:494, appendChange:535, saveMeta:581), and without `withQuotaRetry` (used at 491, 532, 578). The `atomically` doc comment at 1002-1013 states the exact hazard: without the abort, IndexedDB commits whatever requests were already issued, so a throw between the deletes leaves the torn snapshot-gone/header-left state the comment at 696-699 says must never exist. Separately, a transaction abort (quota is plausible since the archive put at 693 duplicates the entry's bytes, and remove has no quota retry) rejects `completed(tx)` after the latch is already consumed; nothing restores it — `expectLoss` is only called from the one-shot `local-changes-dropped` subscription at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:126-128 — so a retried removal takes the `losing === false` ordinary-detach path and deletes the user's only copy of unsent work without archiving. Blocking under the correctness lens as a data-loss / broken-invariant defect. The reviewer's illustrative ordering ("snapshot deleted while the archive put never happened") is inexact, since the put precedes the deletes, but the substantive defect (non-atomic multi-request write, latch consumed pre-commit) is real and that inaccuracy does not meet the refutation bar.
